topics.name: Weights, activations and matrix operations
topics.why: Inference executes fixed learned weights on changing activations; this distinction grounds memory and compute reasoning.
topics.outcomes: weights versus activations; linear layer as matrix multiplication; why a nonlinearity matters.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Multiply a two-input vector by a 2×2 weight matrix on paper or in Python; alter one weight. Free, CPU only.

topics.completionCheck: Identify which values persist across requests and which depend on input.

topics.name: Loss, gradients and training versus inference
topics.why: Adaptation changes weights; ordinary generation does not.
topics.outcomes: loss, gradient descent and backpropagation conceptually; train/eval modes; held-out data.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Diagram one training step and one inference pass, marking gradients and updates. Free, no hardware.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why a prompt at inference time does not itself update weights.

topics.name: Tokens, vocabularies and context
topics.why: Token boundaries determine sequence length, context use and generation granularity.
topics.outcomes: text versus token IDs; subword/byte segmentation; special tokens and chat templates.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Compare code, punctuation and multilingual text in the browser tokenizer; estimate effects on context. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why character count differs from token count and what a special token can signal.

topics.name: Token embeddings and hidden states
topics.why: Initial token vectors are learned lookups; later layers make them contextual, unlike standalone retrieval embeddings.
topics.outcomes: embedding-table lookup; vector dimension; position information; token versus contextual versus sentence embedding.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Trace one token ID into a vector and sketch what later layers change. Free browser; live model may need a capable desktop browser.

topics.completionCheck: Distinguish tokenizer ID, token vector and retrieval embedding.

topics.name: Decoder-only block and forward pass
topics.why: An inference runtime repeatedly executes this path, which explains behavior and cost.
topics.outcomes: embedding → repeated blocks → output projection; attention versus feed-forward network (FFN); residual and normalization roles.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Draw one decoder-only pass and mark which operations mix information across tokens. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Trace the pass including FFN, residual path and output head.

topics.name: Causal self-attention
topics.why: Attention explains how earlier tokens affect a token and why context length costs grow.
topics.outcomes: Q/K/V projections; scores, scaling, softmax and value mixing; causal mask.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Compare attention maps for two short prompts and calculate a two-token weighted sum. Free browser/paper.

topics.completionCheck: Explain causal masking and what attention weights do, without treating them as a complete account of reasoning.

topics.name: Multiple heads, positions and GQA
topics.why: Architecture choices alter both representations and KV-cache size.
topics.outcomes: head splitting; positional encoding and RoPE conceptually; multi-head versus grouped-query attention (GQA); query versus KV-head count.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Compare displayed head layouts and calculate the ratio of KV-head counts with dimensions fixed. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why fewer KV heads reduce cache memory without removing query heads.

topics.name: FFN, normalization and residual path
topics.why: Attention is only part of a block; FFN weights and normalization matter to memory and training.
topics.outcomes: token-wise FFN versus cross-token attention; nonlinear activation; residual addition; pre-norm/post-norm variants.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Annotate token-mixing and token-wise operations on a block diagram. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Explain what the FFN contributes and why a residual path exists.

topics.name: Logits, sampling and autoregressive generation
topics.why: Decoding settings change output behavior while the model predicts one distribution per step.
topics.outcomes: logits/softmax; greedy, temperature, top-k and top-p; feeding back chosen tokens; stopping.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Hold a prompt fixed and vary one sampling control at a time; note probability changes. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Trace two generation steps and explain why lower temperature alone does not ensure factuality.

topics.name: Prefill and decoding
topics.why: Prompt processing and generation stress different hardware resources.
topics.outcomes: parallel prompt prefill; sequential decode; time to first token (TTFT); effects of input/output length.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Change input/output lengths, predict which phase grows, and sketch a timeline. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why long prompts and long responses have different bottlenecks.

topics.name: KV cache and reuse
topics.why: Caching avoids recomputation while consuming memory that grows with live tokens and requests.
topics.outcomes: stored keys/values; cache creation and extension; avoided work; dependencies on layers, KV heads, context and batch.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Use the page's formula to estimate KV bytes for a hypothetical model, stating assumptions. Free calculator.

topics.completionCheck: Explain how caching can improve latency yet reduce concurrency capacity.

topics.name: Context scaling and attention I/O
topics.why: Long contexts increase attention work, KV occupancy and memory movement.
topics.outcomes: standard prefill score matrix; linear KV growth; work versus HBM traffic; FlashAttention tiling.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Sketch full-matrix versus tiled data movement for a short sequence. Free browser/paper.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why FlashAttention does not make attention's arithmetic cost linear in context length.

topics.name: Latency and throughput
topics.why: An optimization matters only for a specified workload and metric.
topics.outcomes: TTFT, inter-token delay and tokens/second; throughput versus request latency; warmup/repetition; prompt versus generation metrics.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Draft a comparison sheet with model, device, token counts, warmup, repetitions and metrics. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Name the metric for first response versus capacity and what `llama-bench` omits.

topics.name: CPU, GPU and memory hierarchy
topics.why: Hardware placement constrains model size and performance.
topics.outcomes: CPU latency versus GPU throughput orientation; compute units, RAM and VRAM/HBM; data movement.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Draw weights, activations and KV locations for CPU-only and GPU-loaded inference. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why capacity and bandwidth can dominate peak arithmetic throughput.

topics.name: Compute-bound versus memory-bound work
topics.why: Choose batching, smaller weights or faster compute according to the bottleneck.
topics.outcomes: FLOPs, bytes and arithmetic intensity; roofline as an upper bound; batch effects.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Vary compute and bytes in the simulator; predict which optimization class helps. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Give one bandwidth-bound and one compute-bound example with assumptions.

topics.name: Select and run a small open-weight model
topics.why: Architecture, license, tokenizer, context, format and device fit are real engineering inputs.
topics.outcomes: parameters versus weight-memory estimate; base versus instruction model; model card/license; RAM/VRAM plus KV overhead.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Inspect a current model card/license, then run a small legal GGUF instruction model with `llama.cpp` on CPU or available accelerator. No API fee; RAM, disk and download required. Fallback: calculate fit from model cards without downloading.

topics.completionCheck: Record model/revision, format, device and context; explain fit.

topics.name: Formats and quantized numbers
topics.why: Packaging and numeric precision shape compatibility, memory and quality.
topics.outcomes: GGUF versus framework checkpoint; FP16/BF16 versus low-bit weights; rounding/scale error; weight versus KV/activation memory.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Enter an outlier and a small value; estimate weights-only storage at two precisions. Free browser/calculator.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why fewer bits need not always improve speed or preserve task quality.

topics.name: Compare quantization choices
topics.why: Bit width alone cannot settle fit, speed or quality for a real workload.
topics.outcomes: weight-only versus weight-and-activation quantization; model-specific sensitivity; controlled comparisons.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: If two GGUF variants fit, use identical prompts/settings and record file size, RAM, prompt/generation speed and output differences. Free local compute. Fallback: compare sizes and memory estimates without asserting quality/speed.

topics.completionCheck: Make one evidence-backed format choice and state what it cannot establish.

topics.name: Static and continuous batching
topics.why: Concurrent requests make generation a scheduling problem.
topics.outcomes: padding and idle slots; iteration-level admission; throughput/latency tradeoff; queueing.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Step through different-length requests and count idle slots. Free browser.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why continuous batching helps and how contention can still hurt latency.

topics.name: Paged KV memory and prefix reuse
topics.why: Serving capacity depends on allocating growing caches across requests.
topics.outcomes: logical-to-physical blocks; fragmentation; sharing/copy-on-write; prefix-cache benefit and occupancy cost.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Map two shared-prefix sequences to logical/physical blocks and show a copy-on-write point. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Explain how paging avoids wasted reservation without shrinking stored KV.

topics.name: Runtime and vLLM anatomy
topics.why: Engines combine model loading, scheduling, kernels, KV management and an API.
topics.outcomes: scheduler/worker/KV manager responsibilities; vLLM batching/paging; `llama.cpp` versus vLLM/SGLang roles.
topics.recommendedPrior: `local-model-choice` for comparing a runtime with a real local setup.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Compare a local `llama.cpp` setup with conceptual vLLM components. Optional vLLM trial only on compatible hardware; no GPU required for completion and free notebook GPU access is uncertain.

topics.completionCheck: Locate request admission and KV allocation; give one reason to choose each runtime.

topics.name: Prefill interference and serving policy
topics.why: Long prompts can stall ongoing decodes even when overall throughput looks good.
topics.outcomes: prefill/decode interference; chunked prefill; TTFT versus inter-token goals; disaggregation costs.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Schedule one long new prompt alongside two decodes under two policies. Free paper/browser.

topics.completionCheck: State a latency/throughput tradeoff and the cost of separate prefill/decode pools.

topics.name: Pretraining, SFT and adaptation data
topics.why: Fine-tuning needs a defined behavior, suitable examples and evaluation target.
topics.outcomes: pretraining versus supervised fine-tuning (SFT); prompt/response data and chat templates; train/validation split; when prompting or RAG is preferable.
topics.recommendedPrior: `local-model-choice` before selecting a model for an experiment.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Specify one narrow behavior and draft synthetic train/held-out examples; identify leakage. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Explain what SFT changes and why the test split must stay separate.

topics.name: LoRA and QLoRA mechanics
topics.why: Adapters train fewer parameters; a quantized frozen base reduces training memory.
topics.outcomes: frozen base plus low-rank update; rank; QLoRA; training memory beyond weights.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Sketch `W + AB`, mark trained/frozen parts, and estimate adapter parameters for two ranks. Free calculator.

topics.completionCheck: Explain why QLoRA is a training setup, not just running 4-bit inference.

topics.name: Guided adaptation and baseline
topics.why: A fine-tuning claim needs held-out comparison with a baseline.
topics.outcomes: a held-out baseline and evaluation rubric; adapter artifact; overfitting and formatting failures; hardware/data constraints.
topics.recommendedPrior: Preview the rubric in `eval-task-quality` before the trial; this later topic is not a gate.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: **Baseline → Adaptation → Re-evaluation → Engineering conclusion.** First define a held-out task set, scoring rubric and baseline evaluation plan using `eval-task-quality` concepts. If compatible hardware is available, record original-model results, run a small LoRA/QLoRA adaptation, test the adapted model on the same held-out cases and settings, then explain differences and limits. A free notebook GPU may be unavailable; check quota, model license and memory before running. Without hardware, inspect the workflow and write an explicitly unexecuted plan and comparison table.

topics.completionCheck: **Conceptual completion:** Explain the data split, baseline, training, re-evaluation and adaptation decision; label all planned results unmeasured. **Hands-on completion (optional without compatible hardware):** Show an actual adapter run, original and adapted model results on the same held-out set, and an engineering conclusion. A plan alone never counts as a completed experiment.

topics.name: Preference data and DPO
topics.why: Preference optimization uses comparative quality labels after SFT.
topics.outcomes: prompt/chosen/rejected triples; reference policy and DPO concept; contrast with reward-model RLHF; label bias.
topics.recommendedPrior: `adapt-lora-qlora` for a later parameter-efficient DPO run.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Draft three preference pairs and find an ambiguous label. Free; training optional/advanced.

topics.completionCheck: Explain what pairwise labels add beyond SFT and what a bad pair teaches.

topics.name: Task-specific quality evaluation
topics.why: Generic benchmarks rarely answer whether a model meets a particular use case.
topics.outcomes: task set/rubric; held-out cases and leakage; human versus model judge; paired comparison and failure categories.
topics.recommendedPrior: `local-model-choice` for a local comparison; `adapt-sft-data` only when evaluating an adapted model.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Create a small private/synthetic held-out set and manually score two variants. Free if a local model runs; fallback: design and review rubric.

topics.completionCheck: Categorize failures and state the limits of a small sample.

topics.name: Reproducible benchmarking
topics.why: Speed and memory tuning require a defined workload.
topics.outcomes: warmup/repetition; fixed model/prompt/settings; prompt versus generation rate; latency percentiles and concurrency.
topics.recommendedPrior: `local-model-choice` for a runnable benchmark; `local-quant-comparison` or `serve-batching` when comparing those configurations.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Repeat local prompt-processing/generation tests with setup and variation recorded. Free CPU acceptable. Fallback: unexecuted protocol. TTFT needs separate end-to-end timing.

topics.completionCheck: Present results with units/setup/limits, or clearly label a protocol unexecuted.

topics.name: Retrieval quality and grounded answers
topics.why: Existing RAG experience benefits from separating retrieval failures from answer failures and comparing adaptation.
topics.outcomes: relevance versus faithfulness; missing evidence versus misuse; context/latency cost; RAG versus SFT remedies.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Reuse an existing RAG pipeline or paper example; manually mark relevant chunks and answer support for a few queries. Free, no judge API.

topics.completionCheck: Diagnose one retrieval and one generation failure with different remedies.

topics.name: Structured output, tools and reliability
topics.why: Valid syntax differs from correct tool choice, arguments and content.
topics.outcomes: constrained decoding and token masking; tool call versus execution; validation, retry and semantic checks.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Define a JSON schema and three syntactically valid but operationally wrong outputs; optionally test a local engine. Free.

topics.completionCheck: Explain what constrained decoding guarantees and what application validation still must check.

topics.name: Engineering decision record
topics.why: The final skill is choosing feasible model, runtime and adaptation/evaluation strategies under constraints.
topics.outcomes: quality/latency/memory/cost; evidence versus assumptions; license/privacy; baseline-to-improvement path.

activities.label: Review the primary resource and learning objectives

practice.instructions: Write a one-page choice for a narrow use case, using measurements if available and labeling untested assumptions. No repo/deployment/paid API required.

topics.completionCheck: Defend a choice with evidence and limitations; name the next test that could change it.
topics.nextHint: An optional deep dive or weak prerequisite.
